Actinic keratoses.summary: A rough or scaly sun-damaged skin lesion that can require treatment and monitoring.

medication_guidance.message: Do not self-prescribe treatment from an image result. A dermatologist can determine whether lesion-directed or field treatment is appropriate.

lifestyle: Use broad-spectrum sun protection and protective clothing.
Avoid intentional tanning and prolonged direct sun exposure.
Arrange a skin examination, especially if the lesion changes, bleeds or becomes painful.

ayurveda.message: Do not replace dermatology evaluation with Ayurvedic treatment. Discuss any traditional medicine with an appropriate qualified practitioner and clinician.

Basal cell carcinoma.summary: A potentially serious skin cancer that requires professional confirmation and treatment planning.

medication_guidance.message: Do not attempt to self-treat a suspected basal cell carcinoma. Professional diagnosis and treatment planning are required.

lifestyle: Arrange dermatology evaluation promptly.
Use regular sun protection.
Do not pick, burn, freeze or chemically treat the lesion yourself.

ayurveda.message: Ayurveda must not replace cancer diagnosis or treatment. Discuss any traditional medicine with the treating medical team.

Benign keratosis-like lesions.summary: A lesion pattern that is often benign, although changing or unusual lesions still require clinical assessment.

medication_guidance.message: Medication is usually not required solely from this image result. A clinician can decide whether removal or another treatment is appropriate.

lifestyle: Avoid scratching or repeatedly irritating the lesion.
Monitor for meaningful changes in size, shape, colour or bleeding.

ayurveda.message: No disease-specific Ayurvedic medicine should be recommended solely from an image.

Chickenpox.summary: A contagious viral illness where hydration, symptom control and prevention of complications are important.

medication_guidance.message: Age-appropriate fever or pain relief may be used according to product labeling or clinician advice. Aspirin should not be given to children with chickenpox. Antiviral treatment may be considered by a clinician for people at increased risk.

lifestyle: Stay hydrated.
Keep nails short and avoid scratching.
Use gentle skin care to reduce irritation.
Avoid close contact with people at high risk of complications while contagious.

ayurveda.message: Ayurvedic products should not replace medical assessment or indicated treatment for chickenpox.

Cowpox.summary: A rare zoonotic poxvirus infection requiring clinical assessment rather than image-only treatment.

medication_guidance.message: Do not self-prescribe antimicrobial or antiviral treatment from an image. Clinical assessment is needed.

lifestyle: Avoid touching or opening lesions.
Wash hands after contact with affected skin.
Avoid sharing personal items that may contact lesions.

ayurveda.message: Do not substitute Ayurvedic medicine for evaluation of a suspected zoonotic infection.

Dermatofibroma.summary: A usually benign skin nodule that often needs no treatment unless symptomatic or diagnostically uncertain.

medication_guidance.message: Routine medication is generally not required for an uncomplicated dermatofibroma.

lifestyle: Avoid repeated friction or trauma.
Monitor for changes in size, colour or symptoms.

ayurveda.message: No disease-specific Ayurvedic medicine is recommended solely from an image.

HFMD.summary: A usually self-limited viral illness where hydration and symptom control are important.

medication_guidance.message: Age-appropriate fever or pain relief can be considered according to product labeling or clinician advice. Antibiotics do not treat the viral cause. Never give aspirin to children.

lifestyle: Drink enough fluids to prevent dehydration.
Use cool fluids and soft foods when mouth sores make eating painful.
Wash hands frequently and avoid close contact while contagious.

ayurveda.message: Traditional remedies should not replace hydration, symptom management or medical review when complications are suspected.

Healthy.summary: No supported skin disease was identified by the model.

medication_guidance.message: No disease-specific medication is indicated from this image result.

lifestyle: Use regular sun protection.
Use gentle cleansing and moisturisation appropriate to your skin.
Maintain adequate sleep, hydration and a balanced diet.
Monitor new or changing lesions.

ayurveda.message: General Ayurvedic wellness practices can be discussed separately, but disease-specific Ayurvedic medication is not indicated from a healthy-image result.

Measles.summary: A contagious viral illness that requires medical assessment and infection-control precautions.

medication_guidance.message: Treatment is primarily supportive. Any vitamin A therapy should be provided under clinical guidance. Antibiotics are only appropriate for bacterial complications.

lifestyle: Avoid close contact with others while infectious.
Rest and maintain hydration.
Follow local public-health and clinician advice.

ayurveda.message: Ayurvedic medicine should not replace medical evaluation or infection-control measures.

Melanocytic nevi.summary: A common pigmented lesion that is often benign but should be monitored for meaningful change.

medication_guidance.message: No medication is indicated solely because a mole appears consistent with a melanocytic nevus.

lifestyle: Monitor for changes in asymmetry, border, colour, size or evolution.
Use regular sun protection.
Arrange professional examination when a mole changes or becomes concerning.

ayurveda.message: No disease-specific Ayurvedic medicine is recommended solely from an image.

Melanoma.summary: A potentially serious skin cancer requiring prompt professional confirmation and treatment planning.

medication_guidance.message: Do not self-treat suspected melanoma with OTC, herbal or Ayurvedic medicines. Professional diagnosis and treatment planning are essential.

lifestyle: Arrange prompt dermatology evaluation.
Avoid unnecessary sun exposure and use broad-spectrum sun protection.
Do not pick, burn, freeze or chemically treat the lesion yourself.

ayurveda.message: Ayurvedic medicine must not replace cancer diagnosis or treatment. Discuss any traditional product with the treating medical team.

Monkeypox.summary: A contagious viral illness for which isolation, lesion care and symptom control are important.

medication_guidance.message: Supportive care and pain control are commonly used. Specific treatment is clinician-directed, particularly for severe disease or people at higher risk.

lifestyle: Avoid skin-to-skin contact while infectious.
Cover lesions as advised and wash hands frequently.
Rest, eat adequately and maintain hydration.
Follow local medical and public-health guidance.

ayurveda.message: Do not use Ayurvedic medicine as a substitute for infection-control or medical treatment.

Squamous cell carcinoma.summary: A skin cancer that requires professional confirmation and treatment planning.

medication_guidance.message: Do not self-treat suspected squamous cell carcinoma. Dermatology assessment and appropriate treatment are required.

lifestyle: Arrange prompt dermatology evaluation.
Use regular sun protection.
Do not repeatedly scratch, burn or chemically treat the lesion.

ayurveda.message: Ayurvedic medicine should not replace diagnosis or treatment of suspected skin cancer.

Vascular lesions.summary: A broad image category that can include different vascular skin lesions with different management.

medication_guidance.message: There is no single medication appropriate for all vascular lesions. Clinical identification is needed before treatment.

lifestyle: Avoid repeated trauma or irritation.
Monitor for bleeding, rapid change or new symptoms.

ayurveda.message: Do not use disease-specific Ayurvedic medication without a confirmed diagnosis and qualified practitioner review.
